info.title: Spotify Data API
info.description:
Spotify data without OAuth: play counts, monthly listeners, artist analytics, the full
catalog (tracks, albums, artists, playlists, podcasts, audiobooks), synced lyrics, credits,
Spotify Charts with daily streams, concerts and playlist change tracking.

## Base URLs and authentication

| Access | Base URL | Headers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Direct API | `https://spotify-proxy.checkleaked.cc/spotify-data` | `x-rapidapi-key: <direct key>` |
| RapidAPI (`spotify81`) | `https://spotify81.p.rapidapi.com` | `x-rapidapi-key: <RapidAPI key>`, `x-rapidapi-host: spotify81.p.rapidapi.com` |

Paths are identical on both: `GET /tracks?ids=…` is
`https://spotify81.p.rapidapi.com/tracks?ids=…` on RapidAPI and
`https://spotify-proxy.checkleaked.cc/spotify-data/tracks?ids=…` on the direct API.
On the direct host, `/docs`, `/openapi.json`, `/openapi.yaml`, `/help` and `/status.json`
need no key.

Every endpoint that takes an `id` accepts the bare 22-character Spotify id; most also accept
a `spotify:…` URI or an `open.spotify.com` URL.

## Errors

Errors use one JSON envelope (`Error` schema):

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "error": "Invalid parameter",
  "message": "\"ids\" must be a comma-separated list of 22-character Spotify track ids (\"abc\" is not one).",
  "code": "INVALID_PARAMETER",
  "status": 400,
  "status_code": 400,
  "retryable": false,
  "param": "ids",
  "example": "/spotify-data/tracks?ids=4cOdK2wGLETKBW3PvgPWqT",
  "request_id": "c0a8012e-5f6b-4a1e-9d43-3f2b7c1d9e10",
  "timestamp": "2026-10-13T12:00:00.000Z"
}
```

Check the HTTP status first, then `code`. A few older endpoints still send only part of
the envelope (for example `{"error": "...", "message": "..."}`), so treat every field
except the HTTP status as optional.

| HTTP | `code` | Meaning | Retry? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `INVALID_PARAMETER`, `MISSING_PARAMETER` | Fix the request; `param` names the field and `example` shows a valid call | No |
| 401 | `MISSING_API_KEY`, `INVALID_API_KEY`, `KEY_REVOKED`, `KEY_EXPIRED` | Direct API key problem | No |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND`, `UNKNOWN_ENDPOINT` | The Spotify entity or the route does not exist | No |
| 422 | `VIDEO_UNAVAILABLE`, `AGE_RESTRICTED`, `PREMIUM_ONLY` | Download endpoints only: the source video cannot be served | No |
| 429 | `RATE_LIMITED`, `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` | **Your** plan's rate limit or quota | After `Retry-After` (`RATE_LIMITED` only) |
| 503 | `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`, `UPSTREAM_THROTTLED`, `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`, `LOAD_SHED` | Temporary problem on Spotify's side, a request that ran out of time (`UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`), or a short overload | Yes, after `Retry-After` |
| 503 | `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` | A request that changes something (POST/DELETE) may or may not have run; `retryable` is `false` and there is no `Retry-After` | No: check its effect first |
| 500 | `INTERNAL_ERROR` | Unexpected server error | Yes, with backoff |

Problems on Spotify's side never come back as 401, 403, 412 or 429: they are answered with
`503` plus `Retry-After`, so a 401 or 429 always refers to your own key or plan.

The API never answers 502 or 504. A request that runs out of time is `503 UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`
with `Retry-After` (it was a 504 until 2026-10). A 502, 504 or 524 with a plain-text body
(`error code: 5xx`) comes from the Cloudflare edge in front of the API. A 504 or 524 means
the edge stopped waiting (a request that ran longer than about 100 seconds): treat it as a
timeout and retry it at most once. Treat a 502 as a retryable network error.

Three documented exceptions to "errors are non-2xx" answer `200`, so check the body too:

- `/track_lyrics`: `{"error": true, "code": "LYRICS_NOT_AVAILABLE", ...}` for a track without
  lyrics.
- `/search_lyrics`: every failure is `{"error": true, "code": ...}`. `NOT_FOUND`: no track
  matched `q`. `LYRICS_NOT_AVAILABLE`: the matched track has no lyrics.
  `UPSTREAM_THROTTLED` or `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`, with `"retryable": true`: the lyrics could
  not be fetched right now; retry later.
- `/album_tracks`: `{"data": {"album": null}, "errors": [...]}` for an unknown album.

Every response carries an `X-Request-Id` header (also `request_id` in error bodies).
Quote it when you contact support.

## Rate limits and retries

- **RapidAPI**: requests per second and the monthly quota come from your RapidAPI plan.
  RapidAPI answers `429` itself when you exceed them.
- **Direct API**: each key has a per-second rate with short bursts allowed (up to twice
  the rate, minimum 10 requests). Above it you get `429 RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`
  and `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` headers. The
  purchased quota is reported in `x-ratelimit-requests-limit`, `-remaining` and `-reset`;
  when it is used up you get `429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED`. Only successful responses count towards
  the quota.
- `503 LOAD_SHED` means one endpoint is briefly saturated; retry after `Retry-After`
  (2 seconds).
- Recommended client policy: retry `429 RATE_LIMITED`, `503` and network errors (including
  an edge 502 with a plain-text body) at most 2-3 times, waiting `Retry-After` (or
  `retry_after_s`) plus a little jitter. Retry a timeout — `503 UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`, or an
  edge 504/524 with a plain-text body — at most once: the request already used its whole
  time budget. Never retry `503 OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` automatically (`retryable: false`). Do not
  retry other 4xx responses.

## Caching and freshness

Responses are cached. Typical freshness: catalog objects (tracks, albums, artists, album
tracks, credits) up to 24 hours; play counts and artist overviews 1 hour; the latest
Spotify Charts 3 hours and past chart dates 30 days; search 10 minutes. The `X-Cache`
header says how a response was served (`HIT`, `MISS`, `BYPASS`, `COALESCED`, ...); values
starting with `STALE` or `FALLBACK` mean a recent copy was served because the live fetch
was slow or failed, and `X-Cache-Stale-Age` gives its age in seconds.

Add `cache=false` to force a fresh fetch. The fresh result replaces the cached copy, and
a given URL is refreshed at most once every 10 seconds (calls inside that window get the
cached copy).

## Slim responses

`slim=1` on `/partner/track`, `/artist_overview` and `/partner/artist-overview` drops the
heavy embedded blocks: the first artist's discography and related content on
`/partner/track` (about 95% of its ~100 KB), and music videos, merch and visual identity on
the artist overviews. Play counts, stats, profile, top tracks and related artists are kept.

## Batch limits

| Endpoint | Max ids per call |
| --- | --- |
| `/tracks`, `/artists`, `/albums`, `/track_popularity_batch`, `/partner/tracks/count` | 50 |
| `/audio_features` | 100 |
| `/album_metadata_batch`, `/track_credits_batch` | 20 |
| `/artist_overview_batch`, `/track_lyrics_batch` | 10 |
| `/artist_compare` | 2-5 |
| `/search_multi_market` | 10 markets |

On `/tracks`, `/albums` and `/artists`, ids that come back without an object are listed in one
of two arrays: `missing` (Spotify does not know the id; asking again will not help) or
`unavailable` (the id could not be fetched this time; retry it later). When no requested id
could be fetched, the call answers `503 UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` with `Retry-After` instead.

## Status and support

- Status page: https://stats.uptimerobot.com/y2392u6LY0
- Machine-readable status: `GET /status` (also `https://spotify-proxy.checkleaked.cc/status.json`, no key needed)
- Support: admin@checkleaked.cc

## Concert endpoints

- `/partner/concert-locations` → search cities/venues, returns `geoHash` + `geonameId`.
- `/partner/concert-feed` → list concerts in an area (paginated). Optional deep-search via `details=true`.
- `/partner/concert` → full concert details by ID/URI/URL (lineup, tickets, venue).
- `/partner/artist-concerts` → upcoming concerts for an artist.
- `/partner/search-concert-artists` → resolve artist by name → upcoming concerts in one call.

Concert endpoints accept `details=true` (parallel deep-fetch, capped by `detailsLimit`,
max 50) and `parsed=true` (flat normalized response shape).

tags.name: Health
tags.description: Liveness and the public status summary. For customer-facing monitoring use `/status`.

tags.name: Charts
tags.description:
Spotify Charts (charts.spotify.com) with daily or weekly streams, plus two Wikipedia-sourced
artist rankings. `country` is an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of a market Spotify Charts covers
(case-insensitive) or `global`; unsupported values return 400 with the list of valid ones.

tags.name: Partner
tags.description: Spotify's internal (pathfinder) data, including play counts.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description:
Playlist change notifications. Webhooks belong to the RapidAPI account that registers them;
they are not available with direct API keys yet.

tags.name: Tracking
tags.description:
Track play-count, follower and playlist changes over time. Tracked items belong to the
calling account (your RapidAPI account, or your direct API key). History starts when you
start tracking an item.

tags.name: AI
tags.description: AI-written analyses built on top of the data endpoints. Every endpoint accepts GET (query string) or POST (JSON body) with the same fields.

tags.name: Internal
tags.description: Operator-only endpoints. Not part of the public API; they require the operator monitor key.

RequestId.description: Unique id of this request. Quote it when contacting support.

RateLimitLimit.description: Direct API only. Burst size of your key (requests it can send at once).

RateLimitRemaining.description: Direct API only. Requests left in the burst right now.

RateLimitReset.description: Direct API only. Seconds until the burst is fully refilled.

ErrorCode.description:
Machine-readable error code. Known values: `INVALID_PARAMETER`, `MISSING_PARAMETER`,
`NOT_FOUND`, `UNKNOWN_ENDPOINT`, `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`, `UPSTREAM_THROTTLED`,
`UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`, `LOAD_SHED`, `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`, `LYRICS_NOT_AVAILABLE`,
`VIDEO_UNAVAILABLE`, `AGE_RESTRICTED`, `PREMIUM_ONLY`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`,
`MISSING_API_KEY`, `INVALID_API_KEY`, `KEY_REVOKED`, `KEY_EXPIRED`, `INTERNAL_ERROR`.
`OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` (HTTP 503) is the one 5xx that is not retryable: a request that changes
something (POST/DELETE) may or may not have run, so it comes with `retryable: false` and
no `Retry-After`; check its effect before sending it again. New codes may be added;
handle unknown codes by HTTP status.

Error.description:
Error envelope. `status` and `status_code` repeat the HTTP status. `retryable` is true
for 429, 5xx and timeouts, except `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`. Older endpoints may send only part
of these fields, and `error` is `true` (boolean) on some of them.

error.description: Short error title (string). A few older endpoints send the boolean `true` instead.

retry_after_s.description: Same value as the `Retry-After` header, when one is sent.

param.description: The query parameter that was missing or invalid.

data.description: Endpoint payload (raw upstream or parsed shape).

ApiStatus.description: Public origin-side HTTP status and usage aggregates. Never includes internal details or customer data; unknown is not an operational verdict.

version.description: Identifier of the API build serving the request.

ApiStatusComponent.description:
One endpoint family. Ids: `catalog` (/tracks, /albums, /artists), `play_counts`
(/partner/track*, /album_tracks), `artists` (/artist_overview, /artist_*), `search`,
`playlists`, `lyrics`, `charts`, `concerts`, `downloads`, `ai`, `tracking`.
HTTP 429, 5xx and aborted responses (499) count as availability failures.
Other caller 4xx are excluded from the availability denominator. No/low samples,
stale or missing recent telemetry are unknown. HTTP rates do not certify payload success.

successRate15m.description: HTTP availability percentage over 15 completed minutes; 2xx/3xx divided by 2xx/3xx + 429 + 499 + 5xx. Null without eligible outcomes.

ApiStatusTelemetry.description: Coverage of persisted origin counters; edge-only quota rejections and requests that never reach the origin are excluded.

ApiStatusMetrics.description: HTTP outcomes are separate from recognized payload/header throttles. Missing series buckets have null metrics; percentiles are histogram estimates.

successful.description: HTTP 2xx/3xx outcomes; includes legacy HTTP-200 error envelopes.

rateLimited.description: HTTP 429 responses observed at the origin.

upstreamThrottled.description: Final UPSTREAM_THROTTLED code or throttle-header responses, including legacy HTTP 200. Null when historical or opaque-response classification coverage is incomplete; recovered internal retries are not counted.

upstreamThrottledObserved.description: Known lower bound of observed throttles even when the exact count is null.

upstreamThrottleCoveragePct.description: Percentage of requests whose final throttle classification was observable.

successRatePct.description: Percentage of all requests ending with HTTP 2xx/3xx.

availabilityRatePct.description: HTTP 2xx/3xx divided by HTTP 2xx/3xx + 429 + 499 + 5xx, as a percentage.

ApiStatusAnalytics.description: Documented customer data/AI/tracking routes only. Operational, credential and webhook paths are excluded. Summaries may be partial; inspect telemetry coverage.

rpm.description: Requests in the latest completed minute after the five-second flush grace.

endpoints.description: Allowlisted normalized endpoint labels and metrics over the last 15 completed minutes.

TrackPlayCount.description: Lifetime play count of one track. Spotify reports 0 for tracks with fewer than 1,000 plays.

tracks.description: One entry per requested id, in request order.
One entry per requested id, in request order.

missing.description: Requested ids Spotify does not have (`status` `not_found`).

unavailable.description: Requested ids that could not be answered this time (`status` `error`). Ask again later.

IncludeStatus.description: Per requested `include` option, how many objects asked for it and how many got a value.

items.description: A Web API track object, plus `insights` / `playcount` when requested.

artists.description: One entry per requested id, in request order.

weight.description: Mean weight over the artist's top tracks (0-1).

tracks.description: How many of the top tracks carry the tag.

basis.description: What the figures are computed from.

relinked_to.description: Set when Spotify serves another track id for this one (relinking): `id` is the id it serves. /tracks reports a relink from the other side (there `id` is the served id and `linked_from.id` the requested one).

error.description: Why an `error` entry could not be answered.

playcount.description: Lifetime plays. Spotify reports 0 for tracks with fewer than 1,000 plays.

releaseDate.description: Release date of the track's album (YYYY-MM-DD, or a coarser precision).

WebAPIError.description:
Spotify Web API style error, used by `/tracks/{id}`: Spotify's own `error` object
(`{ status, message }`, what Web API clients read; `error.status` repeats the HTTP status)
with the standard error fields beside it. The 404 carries `code`, `retryable` and
`request_id`; the 400 and 503 bodies carry every field of the error envelope.

retry_after_s.description: Same value as the `Retry-After` header, when one is sent.

MarketParam.name: market
MarketParam.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. Filters availability and relinks tracks for that market.

ChartIncludeParam.name: include
ChartIncludeParam.description:
Comma-separated extra data in every entry's `trackMetadata` (each option adds time; a
value that could not be fetched is `null`). The body stays a list, so the
`X-Include-Status` header reports `option=resolved/requested` (on a freshly built
response; a copy served from the cache carries the extras without the header):
- `insights`: genres, moods, activities, tags, `bpm`, `credits`, `has_lyrics`,
  `languages` per track (as `/tracks?include=insights`; about +1-4 s for 200 entries,
  cached 24 h per track).
- `playcount`: lifetime plays per track (the entry's own `rankingMetric` is the chart
  period's streams; about +3-8 s for 200 entries the first time, cached 1 h).

CacheParam.name: cache
CacheParam.description: Set to `false` to skip the cached copy and fetch fresh data (the cache is updated with the result). A URL is refreshed at most once every 10 seconds.

SlimParam.name: slim
SlimParam.description: Set to `1` or `true` to drop the heavy embedded blocks (see "Slim responses").

ContrastParam.name: contrast
ContrastParam.description:
Comma-separated list of streaming providers to contrast against.
Appends a `_contrast` field to the response with cross-platform matching data.
Available providers: `ytmusic`, `applemusic`, `amazonmusic`, `tencentmusic`, `pandora`, `gaana`.

DetailsParam.name: details
DetailsParam.description: Enrich each concert with full concert details in parallel.

DetailsLimitParam.name: detailsLimit
DetailsLimitParam.description: Max concerts to enrich per request (max 50).

ParsedParam.name: parsed
ParsedParam.description: Return a flat, normalized concert shape instead of raw GraphQL.

ChartCountryParam.name: country
ChartCountryParam.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of a Spotify Charts market (case-insensitive) or `global`. Invalid values return 400 listing the valid ones.

ChartDateParam.name: date
ChartDateParam.description: Chart date (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to the latest published chart. If that date has no chart, up to 7 earlier dates are tried (weekly charts snap to Thursdays).

ChartCityParam.name: city
ChartCityParam.description: Top 200 tracks only. City chart instead of a country chart (for example `saopaulo`). Spaces are ignored.

AiLanguageParam.name: language
AiLanguageParam.description: Language of the generated analysis (for example `en`, `es`).

AiShowPromptParam.name: showPrompt
AiShowPromptParam.description: Include the prompt that was sent to the model in the response.

example.message: "ids" must be a comma-separated list of 22-character Spotify track ids ("abc" is not one).

Unauthorized.description:
Missing, invalid, revoked or expired key (`MISSING_API_KEY`, `INVALID_API_KEY`,
`KEY_REVOKED`, `KEY_EXPIRED`). On RapidAPI this response comes from the RapidAPI gateway
and has its own body.

example.message: The API key is not valid. Check the x-rapidapi-key header.

NotFound.description: The Spotify entity does not exist (`NOT_FOUND`) or the route is unknown (`UNKNOWN_ENDPOINT`).

Unprocessable.description: The source video cannot be served (`VIDEO_UNAVAILABLE`, `AGE_RESTRICTED`, `PREMIUM_ONLY`). Retrying will not help.

RateLimited.description:
Your own rate limit or quota (`RATE_LIMITED`, `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`). Retry `RATE_LIMITED`
after `Retry-After`; `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` needs a plan change. On RapidAPI this response
comes from the RapidAPI gateway and has its own body.

example.message: Rate limit exceeded for this key. Retry after 1 second.

Overloaded.description:
Temporary problem on Spotify's side (`UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`, `UPSTREAM_THROTTLED`), a
request that ran out of time (`UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`; a 504 before 2026-10) or a short
overload (`LOAD_SHED`). Retry after `Retry-After` (retry a timeout at most once). When a
recent copy of the response exists it is served with `200` instead.

value.message: Spotify did not answer this request. Retry in a few seconds.

timeout.summary: The request ran out of time

value.message: The request did not complete within its time budget. Please retry shortly.

get.description: Liveness check of the API process. Never served from cache.

Public origin-side HTTP status and usage per endpoint family, including RPM, normalized
endpoint rows, error/cache rates, approximate latency percentiles, 60 completed-minute
points and 24 completed-hour points. Completed buckets have a five-second flush grace.
Missing data remains unknown/null, never zero or healthy. Ordinary snapshots are cached
for 30 seconds; stale/unavailable snapshots use no-store. HTTP outcome rates do not
certify payload success; recognized legacy HTTP-200 upstream throttles are counted
separately. The same document is available without a key at
`https://spotify-proxy.checkleaked.cc/status.json`; the human-readable status page is
https://stats.uptimerobot.com/y2392u6LY0.

timeout
parameters.description:
Time limit per search attempt, in milliseconds. It can only shorten a search: `/search`
makes at most two attempts of up to 8 seconds each and answers within about 20 seconds,
so values above 8000 change nothing.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description:
Comma-separated extra data on every hit of the tracks bucket (`type=tracks` or
`multi`), added next to the hit's `data` fields; other buckets are unchanged (400 with
`search_top_results=true`, whose body has no tracks bucket). A value
that could not be fetched is `null` and `include_status` reports `{requested, resolved}`:
- `playcount`: lifetime plays as a number (about +0.5-1 s for 10 tracks, cached 1 h).
- `insights`: genres, moods, activities, tags, `bpm`, `credits`, `has_lyrics`,
  `languages` (as `/tracks?include=insights`; about +0.1-0.3 s).

get.description: Mixed top hits (artists, tracks, albums, playlists, podcasts) in `topResultsV2.itemsV2`.

Searches Spotify for the track, then returns lyrics from Spotify, LRCLIB, or lyrics.ovh, with
the matched `track`. Successful payloads include the provider in `source`.

Failures also answer `200`, with `error: true` and a `code`, so check `error` before reading
the lyrics: `NOT_FOUND` when no track matched `q`, `LYRICS_NOT_AVAILABLE` when the matched
track has no lyrics, and `UPSTREAM_THROTTLED` or `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` with
`retryable: true` when the lyrics could not be fetched right now (retry later).

200.description:
Lyrics with the matched `track`, or a failure: `error: true` with `code` `NOT_FOUND`,
`LYRICS_NOT_AVAILABLE`, `UPSTREAM_THROTTLED` or `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` (the last two with
`retryable: true`).

get.description: Run the same search in up to 10 markets in parallel. Results are keyed by market code.

Web API album objects (label, UPC, copyrights, tracks) for up to 50 ids. Ids without an
album are left out of `albums`: Spotify does not know the ids in `missing`, and the ids in
`unavailable` could not be fetched this time (retry them later). If no id could be
fetched, the call answers 503 `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` with `Retry-After`. Album tracks list
their own artists (featured artists included) and `preview_url` when Spotify has one.

parameters.name: include

200.description: Album data (with `include=playcounts`, each track item carries `playcount`)

get.description:
Album track listing with each track's play count. An unknown album id answers `200` with
`{"data": {"album": null}, "errors": [...]}`.

200.description: Batch album metadata: `results[]` of `{id, metadata, error}`

get.description:
Web API artist objects for up to 50 ids. Spotify no longer returns genres or follower
counts here for many artists: `followers.total` is filled from a cached artist overview
when one is available and may otherwise be null — or always with `include=stats`, which
also adds monthly listeners, world rank and top cities. `include=insights` adds a genre /
mood / tempo profile built from the artist's top tracks. Ids without an artist are
left out of `artists`: Spotify does not know the ids in `missing`, and the ids in
`unavailable` could not be fetched this time (retry them later). If no id could be
fetched, the call answers 503 `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` with `Retry-After`.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description:
Comma-separated extra data:
- `stats`: a `stats` object per artist — `followers`, `monthly_listeners`, `world_rank`,
  `top_cities` (city, country, region, listeners) — and `followers.total` filled when null
  (about +0.5-1 s for 50 artists, cached 1 h).
- `insights`: an `insights` object per artist — `genres`, `moods`, `activities` (mean
  weight over the top tracks and how many carry each), `bpm`, `country`, `top_track_ids`
  (same data as `/artist_insights`; about +0.3 s).
`include_status` reports `{requested, resolved}` per option; unknown values are null.

get.description:
Profile, monthly listeners, followers, world rank, top cities, top tracks with play counts,
discography summary, related artists and social links. Add `slim=1` to drop music videos,
merch and visual-identity blocks.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description:
`insights`: `data.artistUnion.insights`, the artist's genre / mood / activity profile
and tempo from their top tracks (as `/artist_insights`; about +0.3 s, cached 12 h).
`include_status` reports `{requested, resolved}`.

200.description: Batch artist overview: `results[]` of `{id, overview, error}`

get.description: Albums the artist appears on. NOT PAGINATED: the upstream persisted query is registered without offset/limit arguments, so at most 50 releases are retrievable even when `totalCount` reports hundreds — Spotify's own web player shows the same 50 and loads no more. `totalCount` is an upstream catalog count, NOT a page cursor. Passing offset>0 (or limit>50) returns 400 rather than silently serving page 1 again; the response carries a top-level `_pagination` marker describing the cap.

Playlists where the artist was discovered. NOT PAGINATED: the upstream persisted query is registered without offset/limit arguments, so at most 50 items are retrievable and `totalCount` is an upstream catalog count, NOT a page cursor. Passing offset>0 (or limit>50) returns 400 rather than silently serving page 1 again. The response carries both `relatedContent.discoveredOnV2` (raw upstream) and `relatedContent.discoveredOn` (flattened back-compat alias); entries upstream marks `GenericError` (deleted/private playlists) are omitted from the alias, so its item count is lower by design.

200.description: Playlists where the artist was discovered

get.description:
Web API track objects (with ISRC) for up to 50 ids. Spotify relinks some tracks to another
id in the requested market: the returned object then has a different `id` and carries
`linked_from: {id, uri, type}` with the id you asked for. Ids without a track are left out
of `tracks`: Spotify does not know the ids in `missing`, and the ids in `unavailable` could
not be fetched this time (retry them later). If no id could be fetched, the call answers
503 `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` with `Retry-After`. For a single track, `/tracks/{id}` answers
404 when Spotify does not know the id. `preview_url` (30-second MP3) is filled for most
tracks.

Optional extra data with `include` (each option adds time; see the parameter). Every
option is best-effort: a value that could not be fetched is `null`, never a failed call,
and `include_status` reports `{requested, resolved}` per option.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description:
Comma-separated extra data:
- `insights`: an `insights` object per track: genres, moods, activities and tags with
  Spotify's weights, `bpm`, `credits` (name, role, artist_id), `has_lyrics`, `languages`
  (same data as `/track_insights`; about +0.1 s).
- `playcount`: `playcount` per track, lifetime plays (about +0.3-2 s, cached 1 h).
- `total_tracks`: fills `album.total_tracks` (about +0.1 s).

get.description:
Same as Spotify's `GET /v1/tracks/{id}`: returns the track object itself (not wrapped in
`tracks`). 404 (Web API style error body) means Spotify does not know the id; 503 with
`Retry-After` means it could not be fetched right now, so retry: `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`
(no lane answered) or `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT` (no answer in time; retry it at most once). Every
error this route answers itself has Spotify's `error: { status, message }` object, on
RapidAPI and the direct API alike. The exception is the overload guard's `503 LOAD_SHED`,
which any route can answer and which carries `error: true` (the `Error` envelope): read
`code` before `error.status`.

503.description:
The track could not be fetched right now. `code` is `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` (no lane
answered) or `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT` (no answer within the route budget); `error` is Spotify's
`{ status: 503, message }` object (`WebAPIError`). Retry after `Retry-After`, a timeout at
most once. A short overload answers the overload guard's `LOAD_SHED` body instead (the
`Error` envelope, `error: true`, `Retry-After: 2`), as on every route: read `code` first.

value.message: Spotify did not answer for this track id this time. Please retry shortly.
Spotify did not answer for this track id in time. Please retry shortly.

loadShed.summary: Short overload (any route; `error` is `true`, not an object)

get.summary: Track genres, moods, BPM, credits and preview (batch)
get.description:
What Spotify knows about a track beyond its catalog object, for up to 50 tracks per call:
genres, moods and activities with Spotify's weight (0-1, strongest first), tempo in BPM,
credits with roles (performers, writers, producers), the 30-second preview MP3,
`has_lyrics`, vocal languages, ISRC and release date. Entries come back in request order
with `status` `ok`, `not_found` or `error`; `missing` lists ids Spotify does not have and
`unavailable` ids to ask again later. If no id could be answered the call is a 503 with
`Retry-After`. Each id is cached for 24 hours.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated track IDs, spotify:track URIs or open.spotify.com URLs (1-50). `id` is accepted for a single track.

get.summary: Artist genres, moods and BPM from the top tracks (batch)
get.description:
An artist's sound for up to 20 artists per call, built from Spotify's own genre, mood and
activity descriptors of the artist's top tracks: each tag's `weight` is its mean weight over
those tracks (0 for a track without it) and `tracks` how many carry it; `bpm` summarises their
tempos. `country` is the market of the top-tracks list and `top_track_ids` the tracks used.
Entries come back in request order with `status` `ok`, `not_found` or `error`; `missing` and
`unavailable` list the ids that are not `ok`. Each artist is cached for 12 hours.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated artist IDs, spotify:artist URIs or open.spotify.com URLs (1-20). `id` is accepted for a single artist.

get.description:
Uses Spotify color-lyrics first, then keyless LRCLIB and lyrics.ovh fallbacks. Successful
payloads include `source` (`spotify`, `lrclib`, or `lyrics.ovh`). A track without lyrics
answers `200` with `{"error": true, "code": "LYRICS_NOT_AVAILABLE", "message": ...}`.

Batch lyrics with the same Spotify to LRCLIB to lyrics.ovh fallback chain as `/track_lyrics`.
Each entry is `{id, lyrics, error}`; a track without lyrics is
`{id, lyrics: null, error: "<message>", notFound: true}`.
Tempo, energy, danceability, valence, key and more. Tracks without features come back as `null` entries.

parameters.name: isrc
parameters.description: 12-character ISRC, e.g. `USUG11904206` (case-insensitive; spaces and dashes are ignored). A malformed ISRC returns 400; one that matches no track returns 404 (remembered for about 10 minutes, so a repeat answers at once); one Spotify does not answer for within about 12 seconds returns 503 `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT` with `isrc` and `Retry-After`.

get.description:
The album with this UPC/EAN barcode. Spotify is searched for the barcode as given, padded to
14 digits and, only when those two found nothing, as the 12-digit UPC-A form; MusicBrainz then
matches the barcode to an album name. 404 only when Spotify answered for every barcode form
and nothing matched (remembered for about 10 minutes); when a search could not be completed the
answer is 503 `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` (or `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`) with `Retry-After`, so retry.

Finds the track on YouTube and returns download links in `youtube`. `q` may be a Spotify
track id, a search string, or a YouTube video/shorts URL. Videos that cannot be served
(removed, private, age-restricted, Premium-only, or region-blocked in every region we
download from) answer 422 within seconds. A region lock seen from only one of our download
regions, while the other could not be checked, is retryable: it answers 503
`UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` with `Retry-After` (30 seconds). Search, extraction and upload
share a deadline of at most 70 seconds, below the outer HTTP timeout. Exhausted time
answers 503 `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`; a failed download or storage upload answers retryable
503 `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`, never a successful empty download. Optional alternative-URL
failures can accompany an otherwise successful main download.
When YouTube explicitly rate-limits the download session, new extraction attempts
pause for the provider cooldown. The endpoint answers 503 `UPSTREAM_THROTTLED`
with the remaining wait in `Retry-After`; already stored downloads remain available.
